extracted.intended_audience: readers, potential subscribers, advertisers, and contributors to The Forerunner (early-20th-century progressive/women's movement audience)
extracted.subtask_description: Publisher's statement of purpose, content scope, departmental limits, advertising policy, and subscription value for The Forerunner, a monthly magazine entirely written and published by Charlotte Perkins Gilman. Describes what will be published, what will not be answered, ad acceptance criteria, and promised yearly deliverables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of The Forerunner (editorial aims)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is to stimulate thought: to arouse hope, courage and impatience; to offer practical suggestions and solutions, to voice the strong assurance of better living, here, now, in our own hands to make.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The magazine's content should provoke thought and action, offer practical remedies and constructive proposals, and communicate confidence about improving present life. Material ought to support these aims rather than merely entertain or amuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-author publication requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The magazine is written entirely by Charlotte Perkins Gilman.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All regular content (stories, essays, sermons, reviews, departments) is authored by the publisher; submissions or external authors are not indicated as part of the plan for the magazine's issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial scope — subject matter and human focus
rubrics_metrics.description: It is about people, principles, and the questions of every-day life; the personal and public problems of to-day. It will treat all three phases of our existence—male, female and human. It will discuss Man, in his true place in life; Woman, the Unknown Power; the Child, the most important citizen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferred topics are practical, sociological, domestic and civic issues that illuminate human life and social change. Content that focuses narrowly on trivialities or purely decorative matters is out of step with the magazine's remit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ideological stance / relation to Socialism
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a magazine for humanity, and humanity is social. It holds that Socialism, the economic theory, is part of our gradual Socialization, and that the duty of conscious humanity is to promote Socialization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the magazine serves humanity broadly, its editorial line explicitly recognizes and supports socialization and will include material consistent with that perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content types and regularity promised
rubrics_metrics.description: The Forerunner is a monthly magazine, publishing stories short and serial, article and essay; drama, verse, satire and sermon; dialogue, fable and fantasy, comment and review. The first year will include one complete novel, one new book, twelve short stories, twelve-and-more short articles, twelve-and-more new poems, twelve short sermons, plus comment and review and the Personal Problems department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issues should include a mix of fiction and nonfiction forms as listed and deliver the promised yearly quantity of each genre; editors/authors should plan to meet those counts to justify subscription claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal Problems department scope and exclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The department of 'Personal Problems' does not discuss etiquette, fashions or the removal of freckles. Foolish questions will not be answered, unless at peril of the asker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions accepted should be substantive personal or social problems amenable to the magazine's practical, humanistic approach; trivial, frivolous, or merely cosmetic queries are to be rejected or ignored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising policy — experiential and truthful descriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: In its advertising department... will be described articles personally known and used. So far as individual experience and approval carry weight, and clear truthful description command attention, the advertising pages of The Forerunner will be useful to both dealer and buyer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferred ads are those grounded in actual personal experience and clear, truthful descriptions. Advertising copy should aim to be informative and honest rather than exaggerated or deceptive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising acceptance — editor's truth judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: If advertisers prefer to use their own statements The Forerunner will publish them if it believes them to be true.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editor reserves the right to accept or reject advertiser-supplied copy based on an assessment of its truthfulness; unsubstantiated or untrue claims may be refused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscription value and promised deliverables (price vs. content)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you take this magazine one year you will have: One complete novel, One new book, Twelve short stories, Twelve-and-more short articles, Twelve-and-more new poems, Twelve Short Sermons, Besides 'Comment and Review' and 'Personal Problems' and many other things. Price: $1.00 a year, .10 a copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subscription sales and renewal appeals should be justified by the concrete list of deliverables; the price point is explicitly set and used in promotional appeals (renew, recruit new subscribers, gift subscriptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial selection standard — seriousness, usefulness and social worth
rubrics_metrics.description: The Forerunner is to stimulate thought and offer practical suggestions and solutions; it gives a clear, consistent view of human life and how to live it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selections should prioritize work that is constructive, educational, socially conscious, and helpful in changing conditions—material purely decorative or escapist is out of alignment with the magazine's declared mission.
